messages:
From: Lisa Park <lisa.park@trustaudit.com>

Cc: security@finnorth.com
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Initial evidence ask: scan cadence + remediation SLA mapping

Hannah,

Thanks for taking this on. For the SOC 2 fieldwork we need a concise mapping that shows:
- scheduled scan cadence (dynamic/static inventory)
- SLA windows for CVE remediation by severity (what you commit to for FinNorth)
- where we can pull machine-readable evidence (CSV/CSV+SHA zip) on a rolling weekly basis

Can you confirm the commitments and either attach a sample export or a link to where auditors can pull the weekly snapshot? We will use this to validate the control that vulnerabilities are discovered and remediated within your stated SLAs.

A couple of clarifying asks:
1) Do you run authenticated scans against customer-facing infra vs internal infra?
2) For Critical CVEs, what is your escalation path and SLA (business hours vs 24/7)?

Appreciate a short reply with the plan and attachments.

—Lisa
Lisa Park, Senior Auditor
TrustAudit LLP
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Park <lisa.park@trustaudit.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial evidence ask: scan cadence + remediation SLA mapping

Hi Lisa — thanks for the clear list. Below is our proposed single-page playbook covering FinNorth's scope. I attached a sample CSV export and a consolidated PDF rollup for the last scan window.

Summary (high level):
- Scan cadence:
  • External-facing services: authenticated + unauthenticated full scan weekly
  • Internal infra (customer-segment control plane): authenticated scan every 2 weeks, vulnerability delta monitoring daily
  • Container images / CI: vulnerability gating on every build + weekly image fleet sweep

- CVE remediation routing & SLAs (FinNorth commitment):
  • Critical (active exploit or RCE): 24 hours initial triage, incident-level escalation, fix or mitigation within 5 business days
  • High (privilege escalation, exploitable path): 3 business days initial triage, fix or mitigation within 21 calendar days
  • Medium: 10 business days initial triage, prioritized backlog with fixes within 45 calendar days
  • Low: tracked in monthly backlog and reviewed during monthly cadence

- Evidence feed: weekly incremental snapshot uploaded to a secured S3 bucket (link above) plus a CSV export attached. CSV includes: rule_id, cve, severity, discovered_at, status, assigned_owner, patch_window, evidence_url

- Authenticated scans: yes for both customer-facing and internal infra where creds/agents are permitted (we use tokenized scanner creds and agent-only keys for internal hosts). For container images we rely on build-time scanning plus orchestration-level sampling.

- Escalation path for Critical: PagerDuty alert to Security on-call -> Eng lead -> Product security director. We run tabletop drills quarterly.

Attachments: finnorth-vm-scan-inventory-20261221.csv, cve-remediation-rollup-20261221.pdf

Next steps I propose: Kimberly to confirm that the CSV schema is stable for exporters/auditors; Ben to add the signed S3 access policy and final upload. If that looks good I will upload a weekly snapshot tomorrow morning.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Manager, Security Assurance
Redwood Inference

Thanks Hannah — confirming two operational notes for auditors:

1) CSV schema stable as of 2026-12-01. Field list (for clarity) — rule_id, cve_id, severity, discover_ts, host, service, status (open/in_progress/fixed), owner_email, remediation_plan, remediation_target_date, evidence_link

2) Access: we will provide S3 pre-signed URLs for the weekly snapshot. For auditors needing programmatic pulls we can provide a short-term IAM role with read-only listing for the finnorth prefix. Ben, can you attach the S3 policy we discussed?

Also addressing Lisa's authenticated scan question: any externally facing customer endpoints are scanned with credentialed checks where the customer gives permission; internal control plane assets have agent-based authenticated scanning.

—Kimberly
